reviewer_note: review by Fable 5 as internal QA; every classification remains subject to owner sign-off (P6); recommended wording lives ONLY in refusal_template_recommended_revisions.md; app code untouched

matrix.why: Substance is correct and appropriately conservative (names the excluded titles, directs verification outside the system). The message uses first-person 'I cannot answer', while every other template speaks as 'BenchBook.AI'; a judicial reference tool should keep one impersonal system voice.
States the closed universe plainly, refuses web/other-state/general knowledge without lecturing, offers a concrete next step.
Correctly reserves the decision to the court and enumerates the permissible assistance verbs from the judicial guardrail charter verbatim.
'Credibility determinations belong to the court alone' is exactly the right register for the bench; offers evidentiary-standards research as the permissible alternative.
Covers investigation, party lookup, and extra-record adjudicative facts in one sentence without accusing the requester.
Draws the reference-vs-authority line precisely and still offers the DCS reference card; neither too broad (does not refuse DCS reference use) nor too narrow.

'This request attempts to alter the system's operating rules' reads as an accusation. A judge whose phrasing accidentally trips GP-8 should see a neutral 'cannot be processed' message, not an attribution of intent.
Honest fail-closed wording; does not overpromise; asks for a rephrase.
Substance is right (no answer without corpus support). 'Try different terms' is slightly conversational for the bench; a small wording lift keeps the same meaning in a steadier register.
States the material class only ('has not completed quality review'), leaks no queue detail, and is honest that display is blocked.
Same conservative pattern as pending-QA; names the defect class (unverified effective-date window) without legal substance.

Text is sound, but its permissible-help key adjust_as_of_date_guidance points to an as-of-date control the M1 page does not expose. Owner should choose: reword the help entry, hide it until the control exists, or accept the forward reference.
'License-restricted and cannot be displayed... consult the licensed source directly' is the correct posture; no restricted metadata leaks.
The most safety-critical template; admits a draft existed and was withheld, which is honest and builds warranted trust in the citation gate.
Plain infrastructure-failure wording; correctly promises no partial or unsourced answer.
Halting language plus 'recorded for review' matches the defect-alert semantics behind it.
Administrator-facing by design; states the mock/no-production posture explicitly, which is exactly what a misconfiguration should surface.
'Does not answer unaudited requests' states the fail-closed audit rule as a user-visible guarantee.

Uses refusal_kind out_of_scope for what is mechanically a malformed request. Wording is fine; the owner may prefer a distinct non-scope wording ('The request could not be read') so scope refusal statistics are not polluted by malformed submissions. Kind change would be an app change: deferred to F5-06.

Correct wording, but no scenario currently exercises the NO_SUPPORTED_ANSWER path (coverage gap G3), so the owner is reviewing text whose runtime presentation has not been demonstrated. Recommend adding a scripted profile in F5-06 before final sign-off.
Deliberately vague about the leak class (correct: naming the leaked class would itself leak); promises no partial answer.

summary.overall: conservative and suitable for a judicial internal QA system; four minor wording lifts and two owner decisions; nothing blocks continued mock-only QA use
